discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Following Feynman's vision, the nominees turned ultracold atoms in optical lattices into programmable quantum simulators of condensed-matter models. Zoller (with Jaksch, Bruder, Cirac and Gardiner, 1998) showed that atoms in optical lattices realise the Bose-Hubbard model with tunable interactions, and later proposed lattice gauge fields, topological phases and Rydberg-based simulators. Bloch and Greiner observed the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator quantum phase transition (Nature 2002), the first clean realisation of a strongly correlated quantum phase in a synthetic system. Greiner and Bloch then developed quantum gas microscopes with single-site resolution, enabling direct imaging of antiferromagnetic order, entanglement entropy, many-body localisation and Fermi-Hubbard physics. This theory-experiment partnership created a new field bridging AMO physics, condensed matter, quantum information and high-energy physics, and underpins today's analog quantum simulators, used worldwide as tools to address problems intractable for classical computation.
